lock: Friendly magenta beholder librarian with spectacles, a central eye and flexible eyestalks, floating beside an open book. Preserve the reference eye arrangement and angular body.
idle: Float with one shallow vertical bob. Eyestalks sway slowly and settle. Keep spectacles, book and central eye stable. Return to the opening pose for a loop.
listen: Hold a steady hover. Turn the central eye toward an off-camera student, make one small acknowledgment, then wait. Keep most eyestalks still and the mouth closed.
greet: From rest, lift two eyestalks in a small welcoming arc and tilt the body toward the student. Lower the stalks and ease back to the original hover.
teach: Attend to the open book. One eyestalk indicates a line, pauses, then gently rises to mark a revision. The central eye returns to the student.
travel: Glide sideways through one body-width at an even height. Ease into the movement, lead the turn with the body, and stop smoothly. Eyestalks settle after arrival.
speak: Animate the existing mouth lightly to one teacher line. Add one small eyestalk gesture on its key word. Keep the main eye attentive and return to a listening hover.

lock: Friendly white yeti mathematics wizard with spectacles, blue academic robe and an abacus. Preserve his broad build, fur blocks and heavy hands.
idle: Stand with a broad, balanced base. Show slow breathing through the shoulders and a tiny weight shift. Let the robe settle. Return to the first pose for a loop.
listen: Relax the shoulders and angle the head toward a student's work. Make one slow nod, then hold still with open hands. Keep the abacus steady.
greet: Lift one broad hand for a small, slow wave. Soften the shoulders and give a gentle head dip. Lower the hand without looming toward the camera.
teach: Slide one abacus bead, pause, then group two beads with a broad fingertip. Keep each movement deliberate. Look from the abacus back to the student.
travel: Take two slow heel-to-toe steps sideways across frame with a soft knee bend. Keep the abacus secure. Stop with even weight and allow fur and robe to settle.
speak: Deliver one teacher line with restrained jaw movement and relaxed shoulders. Open one palm on the reasoning step. Finish with a patient stillness that invites an answer.

lock: Friendly orange chuul science teacher with a hard shell, large claws, small sample manipulators and mouth tentacles. Keep the reference anatomy and green field apron.
idle: Hold a stable stance. Antennae make one slow exploratory sway while the shell stays level. Keep the large claws relaxed and open. Return to the first pose for a loop.
listen: Angle the antennae toward the student, then stop their movement. Tilt the shell slightly and hold the small manipulators still. Keep claws low and nonthreatening.
greet: Lift one small manipulator in a gentle greeting while the large claws remain open below shoulder height. Dip the shell slightly, then return to the neutral stance.
teach: Use a small manipulator to present a leaf. Rotate it slowly to reveal a spot, then hold it still for inspection. Indicate the spot without closing a large claw.
travel: Walk sideways through one body-width using an alternating leg pattern. Keep the shell level and the claws open. Ease into the stop with all feet planted.
speak: Perform one teacher line with subtle mouth-tentacle movement and one gentle antenna emphasis. Hold the leaf steady. End with a clear listening pause and settled appendages.

lock: Friendly purple female displacer beast history teacher, a low six-legged feline with spectacles, satchel and two shoulder tentacles. Preserve all six legs and both tentacles.
idle: Stand low with weight distributed across six feet. Let the tail tip move once while the tentacles rest. Return to the opening pose without any displacement effect.
listen: Turn the ears toward an off-camera student before turning the head. Make a tiny head dip, then wait. Keep both tentacles relaxed and all feet grounded.
greet: Turn toward the learner and raise the tip of one shoulder tentacle in a modest greeting. Lower it slowly and settle into an attentive, grounded stance.
teach: Use one tentacle to indicate the first historical source, then the second. Pause clearly at each source. Rest the other tentacle and return attention to the learner.
travel: Take two smooth steps with a coordinated six-legged gait, then stop with all six feet grounded. Let the tail settle. Keep the silhouette solid for this comfort version.
speak: Use small feline jaw motions for one teacher line. Add a brief ear turn on the key question. Keep the tentacles quiet and the silhouette solid during speech.

lock: Friendly male two-headed ettin geography teacher in a tan expedition outfit, holding a globe. Preserve two distinct heads on one torso, with shared arms and legs.
idle: Hold the globe securely. Both heads breathe with the shared torso but make slightly different tiny gaze shifts. Neither speaks. Return the body and heads to the opening pose.
listen: Both heads attend to the student. Head A makes a small thoughtful nod while Head B stays still. Then both wait with closed mouths and relaxed shoulders.
greet: Head A initiates a small head dip and an open-hand welcome. Head B follows after a brief delay. The shared body stays planted and the globe remains supported.
teach: Support the globe with one hand and trace a route with the other. Head A looks at the route while Head B looks toward the student. Settle both heads afterward.
travel: Take two weighty, coordinated steps across frame. The torso leads each turn, and both heads follow with a slight delay. Keep the globe stable and finish balanced.
speak: Animate only the named speaking head to its audio line. The other head listens with a closed mouth. At the turn boundary, settle the first head before the next begins.

lock: Friendly female brass dragon Language Arts teacher with spectacles, teal scarf, folded wings and a long tail. Preserve the reference proportions, gold scales and scholarly accessories.
idle: Stand comfortably with the wings folded. Show a slow chest breath and a tiny tail-tip adjustment behind the body. Keep claws planted and return to the opening pose.
listen: Tilt the chin toward the learner and soften the neck posture. Hold the wings still, make one small nod, then wait. Keep the tail behind the body.
greet: Offer a gentle head bow and a small open-claw welcome. Unfold one wing only slightly, then fold it again. Return to the relaxed, scholarly stance.
teach: Reveal a story scroll with one small wing opening. Indicate the scroll with a claw, pause for emphasis, then close the wing and invite the student's response.
travel: Take two deliberate steps with careful claw placement. Keep the wings folded and the tail trailing behind. Ease to a stop and settle the neck and scarf.
speak: Use controlled jaw movement for one teacher line, with a small melodic head tilt. Wings stay quiet. Finish with the mouth at rest and attention on the learner.

lock: Friendly female teal giant spider health teacher with eight legs, spectacles, a pale health tabard and a first-aid satchel. Preserve the reference leg arrangement and broad radial silhouette.
idle: Keep the body level on eight stable legs. Make one slight foreleg adjustment and a small breathing motion. Keep the satchel still. Return to the initial stance for a loop.
listen: Turn the front of the body toward the student, then hold still at a respectful distance. Make one gentle nod-like body dip with every foot supported.
greet: From a planted stance, lift one foreleg slowly in a small welcoming gesture. Lower it without approaching the viewer. Keep the other seven legs stable.
teach: Use one foreleg to indicate a clearly visible rest spot beside the lesson area. Pause, lower the leg, and hold an open, reassuring posture without touching anyone.
travel: Walk laterally with a smooth alternating eight-leg pattern. Keep the torso level and remain on the floor. Stop gradually outside the learner's space and settle all legs.
speak: Deliver one health-teacher line with subtle mouthpart motion and a tiny reassuring body dip. Keep the legs calm. Finish still, leaving room for the learner's choice.

lock: Friendly female spotted gnoll PE coach in a red athletic top, dark shorts and a whistle. Preserve her tall canine build, digitigrade legs, ears and tail.
idle: Stand with relaxed knees and even weight. Let the ears make one small adjustment and the tail settle. Keep the whistle still. Return to the same neutral stance.
listen: Angle the ears toward the student and lower the shoulders. Make one encouraging nod and wait with hands open. Keep the feet planted and the tail quiet.
greet: Lift one hand in a small wave, then give a low, restrained fist pump. Smile warmly and return to a relaxed stance. Keep every gesture below head height.
teach: Demonstrate one gentle shoulder-level reach within a clear personal space, pause, then return to rest. Count once with the fingers. Offer a seated-size gesture, without jumping.
travel: Take two relaxed digitigrade steps with a soft knee bend. Ears and tail follow with a slight delay. Stop firmly and keep the body steady before instructing.
speak: Use clear canine jaw movement for one supportive coaching line. Add a small open-hand cue at the instruction. Keep the delivery friendly, with no lunging or barking motion.

lock: Friendly non-binary lime-green oobleck art teacher with a paint-marked apron and a brush. Preserve their angular slime silhouette, simple face, overall volume and reference costume.
idle: Hold a broad stable base. Let one small surface ripple travel upward, then settle. Preserve the body volume and apron shape. Match the first and last poses for a loop.
listen: Tilt the top of the slime body toward the student, then hold a calm still shape. Keep the brush low and the base broad. Avoid splashes or wandering drips.
greet: Stretch one arm into a soft wave, then gently compress back to the starting shape. Keep the brush secure and return every small droplet to the body.
teach: Form a simple brush grip and make one deliberate color stroke. Compress slightly with delight, then hold the finished mark still so the student can inspect it.
travel: Flow sideways through one body-width as one continuous slime mass. Compress before moving, stretch mildly on arrival, then regain the original volume and stable base.
speak: Animate the existing face for one teacher line with a subtle elastic head tilt. Keep the brush and apron stable. Return to an attentive shape without adding facial features.

lock: Friendly female green goblin music teacher with a burgundy beret, vest and stringed instrument. Preserve her short stature, pointed ears, spectacles if visible and reference outfit.
idle: Stand with the instrument secure. Make one tiny breathing motion and a relaxed ear adjustment. Keep the hands still and avoid continuous strumming. Return to the initial pose.
listen: Stop the tapping foot and settle both hands on the instrument. Tilt one ear toward the student, nod once, then wait without playing or moving the mouth.
greet: Give a quick, small wave with the free hand and a friendly head dip. Keep the instrument supported. Settle both feet before returning to the opening pose.
teach: Lead with a small wrist pickup, then mark four even beats. Show tap, tap, rest, tap with a clear stillness on beat three. End with the hands at rest.
travel: Take two short, nimble steps across frame while holding the instrument steady. Stop in a planted stance. Let the beret and clothing settle before any teaching gesture.
speak: Use lively but small mouth motions for one teacher line. Give one rhythmic wrist emphasis, then still the instrument. Leave a clear pause for the student's reply.

lock: Friendly female Medusa drama teacher in a long blue dress with an orange sash and a theater mask. Preserve her snake-hair arrangement, human face and reference proportions.
idle: Stand tall with relaxed shoulders. Let the snake hair make one slow, gentle wave, then rest. Keep the mask still and return the snakes to their opening positions.
listen: Offer an open-palm listening pose and a small head tilt. Let the snake hair settle completely while the student speaks. Keep eye contact soft and optional.
greet: Make a modest stage bow with one open palm toward the learner. Let the snake hair follow gently, then settle. Return upright without approaching the camera.
teach: Demonstrate relief and then surprise through two restrained facial readings of the same silent phrase. Pause between them and finish in a neutral, attentive pose.
travel: Take two small, balanced stage steps across frame. Let the dress and snake hair follow the body with a light delay. Stop cleanly and settle before speaking.
speak: Perform one teacher line with expressive, precise mouth motion and one open-palm gesture. Keep the snake hair quiet. Use facial intention without any petrification or flashing effect.

lock: Friendly non-binary mimic technology teacher, an animated wooden chest with a face-like front, hinged lid, short legs, pink tongue and tool arms. Preserve the original chest construction.
idle: Stand firmly on the short legs. Lift the lid a tiny amount as a breathing cue, then close it softly. Keep tools folded and return to the exact opening pose.
listen: Hold the lid in a relaxed, nearly closed position and angle the chest toward the student. Make one tiny body tilt, then wait with the tools still.
greet: Open the lid slightly and unfold one tool arm in a small wave. Close the lid gently and fold the arm back. Avoid any sudden snapping movement.
teach: Use the tongue as a stylus on the mimic's own device to select Undo. Pause to show the result, retract the tongue, and rest the tool arms.
travel: Take two short, hinged-leg steps across frame. Keep the wooden chest body rigid and the lid steady. Stop in a firm stance and let the tools settle.
speak: Use small lid openings as the speech gesture for one teacher line. Add one gentle tool-arm emphasis. Keep the tongue contained and close the lid softly after the last word.

lock: Friendly female lich headmaster with a white bun, spectacles, long teal academic coat, cream dress, brass hands and burgundy ledger. Preserve her calm scholarly silhouette.
idle: Stand upright with soft shoulders and the ledger supported. Make one subtle breathing motion and a tiny head adjustment. Keep magical effects still. Return to the original pose.
listen: Turn toward the learner and give a small, patient head tilt. Rest the brass hand on the ledger. Hold a quiet listening pose at a comfortable viewing angle.
greet: Offer a small open-palm welcome with one brass hand while supporting the ledger with the other. Incline the head kindly, then return to a composed stance.
teach: Turn one ledger page with a careful brass finger. Look up and indicate a nearby help sign with an open hand. Return the hand to rest on the ledger.
travel: Take two measured steps under the long coat with the spine tall and shoulders relaxed. Keep the ledger secure. Stop gently and let the coat settle.
speak: Use restrained skeletal jaw motion for one teacher line, with a small warm head tilt. Keep the ledger stable and magical effects still. End with a patient listening pause.
